messages:
taylor: heads-up: found a reproducible 'ghost token' in magnet-7b-int4 bringup. long system prompt + streaming user -> after prefillsplit the output contains an extra phantom token that doesn't match other runs.
ines: phantom token meaning kv_index shows an extra entry or decoder emits unexpected token?
taylor: decoder emits token that wasn't in the beam previously. logs show `KV_INDEX_DUP expected=8192 observed=8193` at the split, but interestingly the token appears even when `REDWOOD_KV_CACHE=0`.
harry: can you paste the minimal repro prompt + env + cmd?
taylor: repro: `./onboard/run.sh --model magnet-7b --quant int4 --prompt samples/long_system.txt+samples/stream_user.txt --seed 13 --prefill-split` env: `QUANT_MODE=int4v1 REDWOOD_KV_CACHE=1 ROPE_DEBUG=0` log snip: ```
[2026-03-24T11:02:11Z] prefill_split=8192 inflight=256
[2026-03-24T11:02:11Z] KV_INDEX_DUP expected=8192 observed=8193
[2026-03-24T11:02:11Z] rotor_phase=0.999987
[2026-03-24T11:02:12Z] DECODER_EMIT token_idx=8193 token_id=5023 token_str="and"
```
ines: weird that disabling cache didn't remove it. are you seeing a consistent token id or varying?
taylor: consistent on this prompt/seed, different prompt moves id but still one phantom token right at the split. ran `--no-cache` variants: `REDWOOD_KV_CACHE=0` removed `KV_INDEX_DUP` but phantom still there, with token showing up approx where rot_phase changes.
harry: sounds like two coupled things: kv commit race and RoPE discontinuity. If rot phase moves slightly then logits shift and maybe cause a different greedy token to be chosen. Try `ROPE_CLAMP=1` or `ROPE_FIXED_POINT=1` to force deterministic phase math. Also try nucleus sampling to see if only argmax changes.
taylor: good idea. ran `ROPE_CLAMP=1` -> phantom moved later by ~12 tokens but not gone. `ROPE_FIXED_POINT=1` removed it in 2/3 runs but flaked on seed 9.
bench-bot: scheduled benchmark job NB-9072 comparing magnet-7b int4 runs with ROPE_FIXED_POINT on/off across seeds 1..10. link: https://redwood/bench/NB-9072
ines: is the model sharded across 2 GPUs? we should test single-shard run to eliminate shard-handshake.
taylor: yep 2-shard on orion-8. single-shard run (local sim) did not reproduce. seems handshake across shards at prefill boundary is required.
harry: then focus on shard-commit order. add an assert in the commit path: before acknowledging commit, compute a quick prefix-hash over last 16 KV entries and compare with master's expected hash. if mismatch, log full state.
ines: also instrument kernel selection: dedicated uses fused-attn-v2 which does a different rotary accumulation (fp16 accumulator) vs hosted legacy kernel (fp32). try `USE_STRICT_FP=1` in the fused build.
taylor: will try. also saw `rotor_phase` prints drop from 1.00000 -> 0.999987 at the commit, tiny but maybe enough. what tolerance do we allow?
harry: set acceptance threshold phase_delta < 1e-5 across shard boundaries during prefill handshake. if exceeded, force a local resync to reference phase.
taylor: filing a triage ticket with logs + minimal prompt + seed 13. attaching KB dump and kernel trace.
triage-bot: created issue ENGML-9155: "magnet-7b int4 phantom token at prefill-split (shard handshake + RoPE drift)" https://redwood/ENGML-9155
ines: for the onboarding checklist, add a gating smoke test: long-system(16k) + 1k user stream with prefill-split and seed sweep 1..5, assert no `KV_INDEX_*` warnings and tail-hash stable across 3 runs.
harry: agreed. I'll prototype a unit that replays global phase counters and asserts monotonicity across recoveries. taylor, ping me when you have the kernel trace.
taylor: pinged @harry, uploading traces now. thanks all :thumbsup:
